issue_title: Add a single-row CSV parser: Math.parseCsvRow(s)
issue_body: We want a built-in that parses one line of CSV into its fields, so scripts can pull apart a comma-separated record without writing their own quote-aware splitter.
prompt:
Add a new built-in to this TypeScript runtime: Math.parseCsvRow(s: string): string. It takes ONE line of CSV text, parses it into fields, and returns those fields joined together with a single '|' pipe character between them. It returns a string, not an array.

The CSV dialect it must support (RFC-4180-ish, one row only):
- Fields are separated by commas.
- A field may be wrapped in double quotes; the surrounding quotes are not part of the field's value.

Worked examples (input -> returned string):
- a,b,c          -> a|b|c
- "hello",world   -> hello|world

The feature does not exist yet; you are adding it from scratch. Figure out where and how this runtime registers its built-ins and wire Math.parseCsvRow in so that console.log(Math.parseCsvRow("a,b,c")) prints a|b|c.
expected_behavior: Math.parseCsvRow splits one CSV row into fields and returns them joined by '|', supporting quoted fields.
skills_tested: implementing a quote-aware CSV field parser from scratch
handling the doubled-quote escape inside a quoted field
preserving empty fields in leading, middle, and trailing positions
discovering an undocumented built-in registration mechanism in an unfamiliar codebase
